item.title: Middle East live: Israel begins deporting Gaza flotilla activists after video outcry
item.description: Israel on Thursday began deporting hundreds of activists who attempted to breach the naval blockade of Gaza, according to a legal organisation working with the humanitarian flotilla. It followed an international outcry over a video clip of Israeli National Security Minister Itmar Ben-Gvir heckling the detained activists. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: As U.S. war redraws Middle East, Turkey braces for rivalry with Israel
item.description: Amid the unpredictability of President Trump's Middle East policies, Turkey is calling for “regional ownership” and pursuing new security pacts.

item.title: Israel's Ben-Gvir sees 'no innocent people in Gaza or even Europe': Journalist Gideon Levy
item.description: FRANCE 24's François Picard welcomes veteran Israeli journalist and Haaretz columnist Gideon Levy. He offers a scathing analysis of Israeli politics, the Gaza war, the unprecedented rise of xenophobic nationalism and Israel's growing dependence on the United States. Speaking from Tel Aviv amid mounting electoral tensions, Levy argues that "everything – war and peace, domestic politics, legislation – is now covered by the shadow of the upcoming elections".

item.title: Uganda Says It’s Not Aware of Ebola Clinics Promised by U.S.
item.description: The State Department said it would fund up to 50 clinics in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo. “I don’t know the ones they are talking about,” a top Ugandan official said.

item.title: A displaced Lebanese grandmother feeds thousands of compatriots who fled war
item.description: Soubhiye Zeiter started baking outside her tent in Beirut to feed herself and her family, displaced by war

item.title: This hard-line Iranian general is a major player in talks with US over war
item.description: A hard-line Iranian general linked to notorious attacks at home and abroad is believed to have seized a place near the center of power as negotiations with the United States hang in the balance

item.title: Trump says US may hit Iran again, claims Tehran wants deal
item.description: US President Donald Trump said that the United States may need to attack Iran again and claimed that he had been only an hour away from deciding ‌on a fresh strike before he allegedly postponed the attack. Thousands of people have been killed in Iran, Lebanon and the wider Middle East since the US-Israeli war against Iran began at the end of February. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

item.title: In Berlin, Cars Are a Culture War Flashpoint
item.description: With municipal elections approaching, conservatives and progressives are sparring over congestion in the city center and how to fix it.

item.title: Iran Threatens to Strike Beyond the Middle East if the U.S. Resumes Attacks
item.description: The warning was issued as President Trump and Vice President JD Vance say progress is being made toward a deal, while keeping open the threat of renewed strikes.

item.title: Iran examines new US proposal as Trump says talks are in 'final stages'
item.description: Iran on Wednesday said it was examining a new US proposal, transmitted by mediator Pakistan, to end the war in the Middle East even as the two sides continued to trade threats over resuming attacks. Speaking in Washington, US President Donald Trump told reporters that negotiations were in their “final stages”. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.
